criteria.criterion: A new file under docs/design/ describes taking each verified job straight to its own pull request without the shared local landing branch, and explains how that removes the landing-and-rebuild wait (Grep for 'landing branch' and 'pull request' in the new file).
criteria.evidence: The only change is the new file docs/design/per-job-pr-landing.md. Its title, section 1 and section 3 contain 'landing branch' and 'pull request'. Section 3 describes cutting each job from the remote main into its own PR, and section 4 explains how this removes the wait. Whether that explanation is sound is covered under findings.

criteria.criterion: The note states the predicted saving of 5.0 minutes per landed job against the 2063.6 median, and says how the next throughput review measures it (Grep for '5.0' and 'next throughput review').
criteria.evidence: Section 6 states '5.0 minutes saved per landed job, against a median of 2063.6 minutes'. It says the next throughput review recomputes the median with StageMinutes::median_of and compares the drop with 5.0. The snapshot status confirms 2063.6 and 1996.9, and the other five stages sum to 37.0. The text meets the criterion, but the measurement method is unsound (see findings).

findings.summary: The measurement method in section 6 cannot score the 5.0-minute prediction, because it ignores the measurement effect that the repository's own notes document.
findings.evidence: per-job-main-landing.md section 1 shows that the headline landing-and-rebuild stage ends at the NEWEST landing record that lists a job's commit (landing_end / landing_record_time .max()). Most of 1842 minutes is later PRs listing the same commit again; the real wait to the first record has a sample median of 4.6 minutes. Removing the shared branch means each commit appears in one landing record, so the headline stage would fall by something like 1900 minutes, not 5. The new note tells the review to 'take the difference in the median per landed job and in the landing-and-rebuild stage' and compare it with 5.0 ('a drop within noise of 5.0 supports the design; a smaller one means...'). It gives no rule for a drop hundreds of times larger, and it would credit the end of repeated listings as saved time. per-job-main-landing.md section 5 already defines the correct method: score the fall in the verifier-end to FIRST-landing-record stage, and do not count a headline fall as savings. The new note should adopt that method.

findings.summary: Sections 1 and 4 explain the 1996.9 minutes as a real serial queue wait, which contradicts the design notes the request cites and the note's own 5.0 prediction.
findings.evidence: Section 1 says 'The queue is therefore serial, and each job's wait is the sum of those before it'. Section 4 says the design removes 'the wait in section 1'. The request says the design notes show almost all of this time is not real waiting, and per-job-main-landing.md measured a first-landing wait of about 4.6 minutes. A reader of sections 1 and 4 would expect most of the 1996.9 minutes to be saved; section 6 then predicts 5.0 with only a one-sentence reconciliation. The note never explains the measurement effect, which is the actual mechanism behind the headline number.

summary: Fail. The new note, docs/design/per-job-pr-landing.md, meets all six content criteria as written. It cites review 20261109-055516-tzwd and states the 5.0-minute prediction against 2063.6. Its numbers match the evidence snapshot (2063.6 and 1996.9, with the other stages summing to 37.0), and every function it names exists in land.rs and pr.rs. Two major soundness problems remain. First, the measurement method in section 6 compares the change in the headline landing stage with 5.0. The repository's own per-job-main-landing.md shows that this stage ends at the newest landing record listing a job, so it is mostly a measurement effect. Removing the shared branch would cut it by roughly the full ~1900 minutes, so the method would credit an artefact as saved time. The method should score the verifier-to-first-landing-record stage instead, as the earlier note specifies. Second, sections 1 and 4 present the 1996.9 minutes as real serial queue waiting, which contradicts the request's premise and the 5.0 prediction. Separately, the expected CHANGELOG.md entry is missing, against the changelog default and the precedent for earlier design notes. That gap conflicts with criterion 6, which allows only added files under docs/design/.
